newsitem.title: UK: World beet sugar output likely to dwindle - Licht.
newsitem.headline: World beet sugar output likely to dwindle - Licht.

text.p: The share of world sugar produced from beet as opposed to cane is likely to continue to fall as it is mostly produced in industrialised nations, statistician F.O. Licht said in a report on Monday.
"One of the features of the world sugar industry in recent years has been the dwindling share produced from beet," Licht said in its first estimate of world 1996/97 sugar production.
"In 1986/87 nearly 37 percent of the world's total was derived from beet -- in 1996/97 we expect the share to have fallen to no more than 29 percent," it said.
Sugar produced from the beet sector in 1996/97 was expected to account for 36.42 million tonnes of the estimated world total of 126.61 million, Licht said.
In 1995/96, beet accounted for 36.43 million tonnes out of a total 123.06 million.
"We believe this trend will continue as beet sugar is mostly produced in the industrialised countries," Licht said.

"The trend could be reversed if there were a recovery in output in Eastern Europe, particularly in Russia, but this hardly appears to be on the cards at the moment." Beet sugar production outside Europe was expected to fall in 1996/97, with output in the two largest non-European producers, the U.S. and China, likely to be down, the Licht report said.
